messages.author: afa289b81aad98c2
messages.subject: geom_text vexeth me!
parts:
Hi All...

I seem to perpetually be frustrated by geom_text, as I can never get
it to perform inside a function. Appended below is test data and a
function intended to draw a box plot, with possible overlay of points,
faceted by a factor. My intent is to display "count = xx" at the
bottom of each facet, but no joy. The function works just fine if you
comment out the geom_text portion. With that section active however,
I get the following error:

Error in r[i1] - r[-length(r):-(length(r) - lag + 1L)] :
non-numeric argument to binary operator

which seems to come from the bowels, but basically means that I'm not
passing something correctly. Modifications of the geom_text details
just leads to different errors.

Does anyone have a suggestion? I did have a working version using
annotate, but the text quality was not good. R-help and ggplot2
archives didn't seem to have anything quite right, but I'm still
learning, so I could be wrong.

A possibly related question: my data is wide; would it simplify things
to melt it? My guess is not, which is why the current version isn't
melted.

Thanks to Any and All! Bryan
DePauw Univ.
Greencastle, IN, USA

********* test data & function call

made.up <- data.frame(R = rnorm(50), F = rep(c("A", "B"), 25))
made.up[c(13, 30, 41), 1] <- NA

compareCats(data = made.up, res = "R", fac1 = "F", fac1cols = c("red",
"blue"), overlay = TRUE, method = "box")

******** the function

compareCats <- function(data = NULL, res = NULL,
fac1 = NULL,
fac1cols = NULL, overlay = FALSE,
method = c("box"),
title = "Comparison of Means", y.lab = "your text here",
x.lab = "your text here") {

# Function to compare categorical data by
# plotting means and se's or something similar
# Bryan Hanson, DePauw Univ, Jan 2010

require(ggplot2)

# 1st, reduce the df and clean it of NAs
# otherwise there is trouble with the counts

data <- na.omit(data)

# Specify the data & aesthetics

p <- ggplot(data, aes_string(x = fac1, y = res, color = fac1))

# now add layers as requested

if (method == "box") {
p <- p + geom_boxplot(width = 0.2)
}

# ... some other methods dropped ...

# now add the common decorations & modifications

p <- p + xlab(x.lab) + ylab(y.lab) + scale_colour_manual(values =
fac1cols) +
opts(title = title, axis.text.x = theme_text(colour = "black"),
axis.ticks = theme_blank(), legend.position = "none")
if (overlay) {
jit <- position_jitter(width = 0.1, height = 0.0)
p <- p + layer(geom = "jitter", position = jit, color = "black")
}

# this next section causes the error

p <- p + geom_text(aes_string(x = fac1,
y = min(res) - 0.1 * diff(range(res)),
label = paste("n = ", ..count.. , sep = "")),
color = "black", size = 4.0, stat = "bin", data = data)

print(p)
}

messages.author: b756a7daa2c2aa6d
messages.subject: Re: geom_text vexeth me!
parts:
Hi Mark,

The key is to think about when you want the calculations to occur.
Currently you have:
y = min(res) - 0.1 * diff(range(res))

That calculation occurs when you run the function because you're using
aes_string. What you want is:
y = "min(res) - 0.1 * diff(range(res))"

that will be converted to the equivalent of aes(y = min(res) - 0.1 *
diff(range(res))) and evaluated when the plot is created. This is the
big difference between aes_string and aes.

Hadley

PS. You'll need to do the same for label = 'paste("n = ", ..count.. , sep = "")'

parts:
Hmm... works for me, even the "n =" labels. I pulled everything apart
and set all the variable values. Ultimately I got to

p <- ggplot(data, aes_string(x = fac1, y = res, color = fac1)) +
geom_boxplot(width = 0.2) +

xlab(x.lab) + ylab(y.lab) +
scale_colour_manual(values = fac1cols) +
opts(title = title, axis.text.x = theme_text(colour = "black"),
axis.ticks = theme_blank(), legend.position = "none")

p + geom_text(aes_string(x = fac1,
y = paste("min(",res,") - 0.1 * diff(range(",res,"))", sep=""),
label = 'paste("n = ", ..count.. , sep = "")'),

color = "black", size = 4.0, stat = "bin")


And it plots with (I think) the labels you are looking for.

The trick to aes_string is that the arguments have to be string
representations of what you want. The string you pass in has to be
understandable down the line. You want geom_text to understand the
value of res, not res as something in a string.

y=min(res) - 0.1 * diff(range(res))

attempts to first process the stuff on the right of the assignment,
where the value of res ("R") does not make sense. Range and diff don't
care about the current data frame, just what they get.
y="min(res) - 0.1 * diff(range(res))"

I am guessing that this may attempt to do the same thing down the line
inside geom_text.
y = paste("min(",res,") - 0.1 * diff(range(",res,"))", sep="")

The value of y is the string "min(R) - 0.1 * diff(range(R))". geom_text
then uses R as the column name of the current data frame, which is what
you want. geom_text wants the column name, not something it should
parse to find the column name.

This is my understanding anyhow. Trust but verify!
